To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of cytokeratin markers in frozen sections is helpful for the diagnosis of basal cell carcinoma and 2) the use of these markers in combination with the routine haematoxin and eosin stain can help in the evaluation of basal cell carcinomas that are incompletely excised during micrographic (Moh's) surgery.
rapid immunohistochemical techniques are useful adjuncts in the histological assessment of basal cell carcinomas.
the cytokeratin markers, LP34, MNFL 116 and NCL-Pan-CK, can be used to identify the basal cell carcinoma cells in frozen sections of the tumour.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of rapid immunoperoxidas and immunofluoroscent techniques to assist the histological interpretation of infiltrative basal cell carcinoma.
the use of rapid techniques to supplement the routine histological evaluation of tumours in Mohs' surgery.
the use of cytokeratin markers on frozen sections to supplement the routine histology in the assessment of basal cell carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of cytokeratin markers on frozen sections can assist in the diagnosis of infiltrative basal cell carcinoma, but that the use of immunohistochemistry on paraffin sections is of no value in this respect.
the use of these rapid techniques is of considerable benefit to the surgeon in the histological interpretation of basal cell carcinoma.

the use of cytokeratins in Mohs' surgery can assist in identifying the margins of basal cell carcinomas, particularly in those cases where the tumours are poorly differentiated, and where the histological features of the tumour may be confused with the surrounding tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of rapid immunocytochemical methods to supplement the routine haematoxin and eosin stains in the histopathological assessment of basal cell carcinoma is of considerable benefit in the evaluation of these lesions, especially when they are infiltrative.

the use of rapid immunoperoxide techniques on frozen sections using the cytokeratin markers, LP34, MN 116 or NCL-Pan-Ck is a valuable adjunct to routine haematoxlin and eosin staining in the evaluation of basal cell carcinomas for micrographic (Moh's) surgery.
the immunohistochemical staining with the cytokeratin markers is of value to the Mohs' micrographic surgeon in identifying residual basal cell carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single cytokeratin antibody that is superior in all cases.
the use of rapid techniques using cytokersin markers to assist treatment of basal cell carcinoma is a good idea.

there is a lot of room for improvement in how we treat basal cell carcinomas, especially in terms of the cosmetic outcome and patient satisfaction, and that the Mohs technique is a promising way of achieving this.
